t.E904.agn: In 2024 EFSA set an ADI of 4 mg/kg body weight/day for physically decolourised, dewaxed shellac; for shellac produced by chemical bleaching it considered this value provisional pending data on organochlorine impurities. It noted that the ADI was slightly exceeded at high consumption in some age groups, but, stating that the calculations were conservative, concluded that this does not indicate a safety concern.
t.E904.body: Intestinal absorption of shellac components is very low; in rats only very small amounts were measured in the blood.
t.E904.eval: Obtained from the secretion of the lac insect (not vegan).
t.E904.found.1: Confectionery, chewing gum and small chocolate-coated bakery products
t.E904.found.2: Surface of unpeeled boiled eggs and coffee beans
t.E904.prod: Obtained from the secretion of the lac insect.
t.E904.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI 4 mg/kg body weight/day (provisional for chemically bleached shellac).
t.E904.summary: A resin obtained from the secretion of the lac insect. A glazing agent in coatings for dragées, confectionery, fruit and medicines.
t.E904.what: A resin obtained from the secretion of the lac insect; used as a glazing and coating agent.
